Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As part of MedSecure's legal review for our vendor DPA we need a concise technical appendix that addresses cross-border transfer mitigations and international safeguards. Our GC team has the high-level ask, but the things they specifically want in this appendix are:

- A data flow table showing where customer data is processed (EU/US/APAC) and which systems hold persistent copies.
- Details on transfer mechanisms used (SCCs/DPF/other) and the fallback policy if a transfer path is unavailable.
- Encryption at-rest and in-flight (algorithms, KMS model) and whether customer-managed keys are supported.
- A high-level network diagram showing ingress/egress points and logging/audit capture.

Can you share a short appendix (1-2 pages) and any supporting artifacts (mapping spreadsheet + diagram) by EOD Wednesday our time? I can coordinate with legal if we need to redline a specific annex.

Appreciate it — Alicia

Hi Alicia — thanks, sending an initial package below.

Attached: redwood-dpf-mapping.xlsx (exports + processing map) — includes per-region processing columns and retention notes.

Quick summary for legal (TL;DR):
- Primary processing occurs in US-hosted inference fleet by default; EU-only hosting available via our Dedicated EU pool or Private deployment (VPC).
- Transfer mechanism: SCCs in place for EU<->US flows; for regulated customers we offer DPF-based contractual terms where required and can support additional safeguards (restricted routing, minimized egress, customer-managed KMS).
- Encryption: TLS1.3 in transit; AES-256-GCM at rest. Customer KMS (Bring-Your-Own-Key) is supported in Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted customers can request CMK with an enterprise agreement.
- Fallback: automatic routing to nearest compatible model variant in-region; if cross-border path blocked, requests fall back to a cached deterministic mode (non-retraining) and are logged for escalation.

Neha / Laura — tagging you for any gaps in the mapping sheet and to confirm whether we should include a short DPA annex template for MedSecure to redline.

Thanks,

Hi Alicia, Rishi — adding the answers below and attaching a short DPA annex draft that covers transfer mechanisms + subprocessors.

1) Data flow table: see redwood-dpf-mapping.xlsx (tab: MedSecure). We mark categories as PII/PHI-derived and indicate whether persistent storage occurs in US, EU, or both.

2) Transfer mechanism: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) are our baseline for hosted transfers. For customers requesting stronger contractual language, we provide a DPF addendum that stipulates EU processing region pinning and detailed logging obligations. The annex draft shows both options.

3) Fallback policy: policy is documented in the appendix — key points: (a) in-region pinning is honored when requested; (b) if pinned capacity met but cross-border routing blocked, we queue requests for a brief retry window (30s) then serve from a certified fallback variant (quantized model) in-region with degraded latency but same output semantics; (c) customers may request synchronous failure behavior in the contract.

4) Encryption & key management: We use AES-256-GCM for storage, TLS1.3 for transport, and HSM-backed keys for platform-managed KMS. BYOK/HSM integration is available for Dedicated/Private. We note caveats for hosted BYOK (requires enterprise network peering).

Attached: dpa-annex-std-answers.pdf, crossborder-territory-table.csv

Laura and Karthik — please review the annex for legal phrasing; MedSecure prefers explicit audit log retention windows and a clause for Data Processing Impact Assessments (DPIAs) on request.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Alicia — quick responses inline to address the outstanding asks. Attaching a network diagram and a subprocessors CSV for clarity.

- Audit log retention: platform default retention for operational audit logs is 90 days. For customers with an enterprise package we can extend retention to 365 days on request (contracted). For export/eDiscovery requests we provide immutable exports within 48 hours.

- Hosted BYOK networking: minimal setup is VPC peering (or private link), egress policy restricting traffic to our ingestion endpoints, and a mutually agreed CIDR allowlist. We also require TLS1.3 and mTLS for control-plane operations. Detailed steps are in the linked guide: https://docs.redwood.inference/internal/dpf-mapping#medsecure

- Subprocessors: see attachment (subprocessors-medsecure.csv). Primary subprocessors are listed (cloud object storage provider for weights, telemetry aggregator, and a managed redis cache provider). We mark which subprocessors have Data Processing Agreements and SCCs in place.

If this looks good we can get legal to exchange a short DPA annex based on Neha's draft and sign off.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
